messages:
rachel: Quick sync — I want to propose a new long-term initiative: 'Topology contracts' to cleanly separate routing, region affinity, and tenant isolation decisions. Goal is clearer SLAs + a predictable migration path for Dedicated/Private customers. Thoughts?
ben: +1. We need concrete launch gates though — customers will ask about RTO/RPO and cost impact.
priya: @rachel I like the name. Can we spell out what a contract contains? e.g. routing policy, eviction thresholds, allowed failover regions, isolation level (soft/hard).
omar: Also need runbook hooks. If a region degrades we should have an automatic step-down path and a manual escalation.
lina: From PM ops: sales told us two enterprise prospects want per-tenant region pinning and predictable worst-case latency. They expect a migration window of <3 months.
ben: Implementation tradeoffs: soft affinity (prefer local, allow failover) vs hard affinity (never leave region). Hard affinity == more capacity fragmentation and cost.
priya: Agree. Proposal: define three contract tiers: "Flexible", "Bounded", "Pinned". Each tier maps to routing behavior and SLA.
rachel: Good. Draft launch criteria I have in mind: 1) policy DSL v1 in control plane 2) telemetry showing region-affinity choices for 90% of traffic 3) failover playbook + canary customer on Dedicated.
ben: Suggest adding perf guardrails: median p95 latency delta < 20% vs baseline when enforcing Bounded.
priya: Ops/infra asks: need a simulation runner to estimate capacity blowup for Pinned at expected tenant mixes. Can eng-ml help with synthetic traffic?
ben: We can wire a synthetic workload generator. Quick snippet for sim config:```yaml
workload:
  tenants: 10000
  heavy_tail: true
  pinned_fraction: 0.12
```
omar: On the SRE side, require SLOs + an automated evacuation path. Also add a telemetry flag for "isolation_mode" per request.
lina: Customer acceptance checklist (short): - documentation + example manifests - SLA table per tier - migration procedure - cost impact estimate
rachel: OK — owners: priya = policy + contracts spec, ben = runtime + sim, omar = runbooks + telemetry, lina = customer docs + migration checklist. Targeting Q3 for alpha with select Dedicated customers.
priya: One more: policy precedence rules — what if customer requests Pinned but capacity absent? We need a fail mode: deny or degrade to Bounded?
ben: Prefer degrade to Bounded with explicit customer consent during onboarding. Denying is harsh for PLG flows.
priya: Noted. We'll add an acceptance flow: if capacity insufficient, system offers "degrade to Bounded" with estimated latency/cost impact and an opt-in toggle.
deploy-bot: scheduled job started: infra/sim-runner-2025-07 queued (job id 9876) :white_check_mark:
rachel: Nice — can the sim-run output be a small report we can attach to the customer proof-of-concept?
ben: Yes, we'll output per-tenant capacity factor + expected cost multiplier. Format will be CSV + small JSON summary.
omar: Final ask from SRE: extract a small set of post-launch alerts: sustained region overload, tenant eviction rate > 0.5%/min, policy-precedence-mismatch.
lina: I'll prepare a short one-pager for sales and get feedback from the two prospects.
rachel: Thanks everyone. Action items: priya spec draft by EOW, ben prototype sim by mid-next-week, omar runbook checklist + alerts by next Thu, lina sales one-pager by Friday. Ping me with blockers. :thumbsup:
priya: Will do. Adding a rough spec branch to the repo tonight.
ben: Starting sim infra tomorrow.
omar: I'll draft the runbook and share early for comments.
lina: Sync with sales this afternoon, will loop you in.
rachel: Closing the thread for now — we'll reconvene after artefacts land. :eyes:
